newsitem.title: HONG KONG: WEEK AHEAD-Limited upside seen for Hong Kong stocks.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD-Limited upside seen for Hong Kong stocks.

text.p: Gains for Hong Kong stocks may be limited in the coming week with many investors on the sidelines awaiting corporate results and news on interest rates, analysts said.
"Sentiment will continue to be cautious, although we could see a rebound at the beginning of the week," said Edward Chan, head of research at Amsteel Securities.
The Hang Seng Index ended 180.56 points or a sharp 1.4 percent lower on Friday at 12,736.53. Turnover was a frothy HK$12.52 billion.
Over the week, the index lost a total of 600.82 points, or 4.5 percent. Turnover averaged HK$12.23 billion a day.
"Interest rate worries are a bit overdone, but many investors may stay on the sidelines until the end of the month," Chan said.
The U.S. Federal Reserve's policy setting committee meets on March 25, and many brokers believe the U.S. central bank may raise interest rates by at least 25 basis points.
Locally, the corporate results season rolls on, and some major upcoming property sales as well as the government land auction on March 25 could give the market direction, analysts said.
Technically, analysts said the index looked oversold but still vulnerable to further downside, especially if Wall Street jitters continued.

"We probably are very close to getting a bounce in Hong Kong, but the bounce probably won't go much past 13,000, maybe 13,200 in the coming week," said Thomas Schroeder, regional technical strategist at SocGen Crosby Securities.
"I think you will get temporary relief from the Dow Jones but I see more downside in the Dow Jones over the next two weeks," Schroeder said.
The local market was shaken by the Dow Jones Industrial Average's 160-point fall on Thursday, its fifth steepest fall in point terms in the history of the average, to 6,878.89.

The U.S. bond market was the catalyst for the Dow's fall. The 30-year long bond closed Thursday trading in New York 30/32 lower at 95-26/32 to yield 6.96 percent, the highest level in nearly six months, and signalling near-term rises for interest rates, brokers said.
On Friday, the Dow rebounded 56.57 points to 6,935.46 but the benchmark 30-year bond yield remained high at 6.94 percent.
The trend in the U.S. long bond has recently set the tone for both Hong Kong and U.S. equity markets.
"At this point I think the bond market has fallen out of bed and has broken critical support," said Schroeder.
Individual investors were active throughout the week and China-related "red chips" often bucked the market's downtrend.
"China plays held up relatively well," said a broker with a Singaporean house.
"The red chips have been riding the theme that the worst in the China economy is over, that the cycle has bottomed out," she said. "But now those red chips are looking pretty expensive."
Strong earnings growth from the Swire group during the week did little to lift sentiment.

Hong Kong Aircraft Engineering Co Ltd started off with a 49.3 percent rise in 1996 earnings, followed by Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd with 27.9 percent net profit growth, and finally Swire Pacific Ltd with a profit rise of 18.6 percent.

In the coming week, the Henderson Land group of companies, the Hang Lung group, Sun Hung Kai Properties and Hopewell Holdings will report interim results. Wharf Holdings and Cheung Kong Infrastructure will report final results for 1996.
